newsitem.title: USA: U.S. shuttle set for July 1 launch.
newsitem.headline: U.S. shuttle set for July 1 launch.

text.p: The space shuttle Columbia is ready for a rerun of a science mission cut short in April because of mechanical difficulties, NASA officials said on Thursday.
Space agency managers, meeting at Florida's Kennedy Space Centre, set July 1 as the launch date for Columbia, NASA spokesman Joel Wells said.
The shuttle will be making a second attempt to complete a 16-day research mission curtailed in April after only five days aloft because of a troublesome electricity generator.
Blast off for Columbia and its crew of seven astronauts was set for 2:37 p.m. EDT (1837 GMT) during a 2-1/2 hour launch window.
The mission's $84 million research programme features 33 major experiments, including several to study the behaviour of fire in space.
Columbia, the oldest shuttle in NASA's fleet, was prepared for the rerun of the mission in near-record time, spending just 56 days in its hangar.
